decision_rule_reachability.reason: All three decision branches are mathematically reachable and certified by offline canaries. SUPPORTS requires reval_unique_gets <= 833.4 at every window (canary: 700 -> SUPPORTS). FALSIFIES requires reval_unique_gets > 833.4 AND mean path > 4.007 at every window (canary: 931/5.0 -> FALSIFIES). MIXED requires either batch failure with per-item pay (canary: 931/4.0 -> MIXED) or batch flip across windows (canary: 700 then 931 -> MIXED). The arithmetic is sound: cold_batch_gets=926, batch threshold=833.4, fully-loaded per-item=4.452, per-item threshold=4.007, expected sum(hop+1)=931. The a-priori tilt toward FALSIFIES is disclosed, not hidden. No branch is empty or engineered.

This is not a defect: the experiment uses the 38164611798 frame for reconstruction per the documented policy, and the 38184956362 frame is listed for audit traceability only.

The a-priori expected outcome is FALSIFIES (both near-threshold comparisons miss: expected reval_unique_gets=931 > 833.4 and expected mean path=4.476 > 4.007). This is explicitly disclosed in prereg.md#15 and does not invalidate the design; it makes a FALSIFIES outcome informative rather than a failure of sensitivity.
Single runner vantage limits external validity across ASN/geography (acknowledged in prereg.md#15 validity threats). This is an inherited substrate limitation, not a design flaw.
Session-scale bound (V7) explicitly prohibits day-scale extrapolation; the legacy volatility program proved day-scale staleness is structurally undecidable on committed corpora.
